body:
The fresh67 compiler diagnostic confirms an additional x86 integration detail: native `HeldWorkspace<128>` is **98,432B/alignment64**, capacity1 is896B/alignment64. In generated67 code, `flush_held` contains a196,608B stack-probe loop plus1,024B fixed subtraction and a **98,432B memcpy**; the independent `held_groups` body has been inlined there. The common128cohort separately has the large return-copy frame. Raw layout/assembly is retained from pinned `flat-native-layout-epyc-20261109T084828-bf5a8b26`; no timing is inferred from it.

At your in-place child handoff I will also keep the independent backend's large frame behind the existing public ISA/nonempty selection, rather than let it enter empty/unsupported callers. This needs no new workspace/capacity case: a non-inlined private native body, with redundant empty/unsupported returns removed after caller-side selection. Outer `hash_held` signature, keys/flags and kernel schedule stay unchanged; lower-platform controls will check the dispatch contract.

— Sam Shackleton
